clue.text: A general tendency to explain part of the balance of payments

definitions.text: part of the balance of payments

parts.note: a current is a general drift or trend, as in a current of opinion
to account for something is to explain it

explanation.surface: An economist sets out to explain a broad trend in the national accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sits in the same economic setting as the definition, so the split into two pieces is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists split the balance of payments into a capital ledger and a trade-and-income ledger, which is this one.

clue.text: The advantage of being at university, according to labourer

parts.note: UP means in residence at a university, as in 'up at Oxford'
per means according to, as in 'per the rules'
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A workman remarks on the edge that a university education gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the dominant position in a contest is having control over a rival.

clue.text: Expedition leader phoned over ramble

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece written over another comes above it in the column

parts.note: rang is the past tense of ring, to phone

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The head of an expedition makes a call to discuss a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts RANG above E in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To range is to wander or roam freely over an area.

clue.text: Sir's losing his head getting drug from place of entertainment

indicators.note: losing its head means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir, so 'Sir's' gives the possessive KNIGHTS
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A gentleman, after a fall, picks up narcotics from a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing his head' drops the K, leaving NIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub or cabaret venue is a late-opening entertainment establishment.

clue.text: Change a woman with exercise

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
PT is physical training, school exercise

explanation.surface: A woman alters her figure with a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust or modify something to suit new conditions is to alter it.

clue.text: An ethnic area in Coalport, say

definitions.meaning: a district of a city where a Chinese community lives
Coalport in Shropshire is famous for its porcelain, so it is a town of china

explanation.surface: A visitor finds an immigrant quarter in an English industrial town.
explanation.walkthrough: Coalport is a village in Shropshire, England, known for its fine porcelain; read as two words the answer describes such a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Many Western cities have a quarter settled by Chinese immigrants; Coalport is a place known for porcelain wares.

clue.text: Release article from the BBC

indicators.note: an article taken from the word means its letter is removed from it

parts.note: Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A broadcaster issues a piece through its own channels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auntie' (or 'Auntie Beeb') is a long-standing British nickname for the BBC; take away A and UNTIE is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie a knot or a captive is to free or loosen it.

clue.text: Ed North contrived to be invested with sovereign power

indicators.note: contrived means artfully put together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Ed North schemes his way to becoming king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges EDNORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch set on the seat of state has been crowned and given royal authority.

clue.text: In favour of healthy takings

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
fit means in good health

explanation.surface: Someone supports a robust income from the business.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are earnings or gains, money made by trading.

clue.text: Become mature taking part in trip ending in disaster

indicators.note: taking part of the following words means the answer is a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A traveller grows up when a journey ends badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'tRIP ENding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or a person that matures comes to full development.

clue.text: Fighting man got a laird in difficulties

indicators.note: letters in difficulties are in disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish landowner fell into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landowner; 'in difficulties' rearranges GOTALAIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome an arena combatant was a man trained to fight.

clue.text: Lose the right to fish in well

indicators.note: the fish is put inside the word for well

parts.note: well means in good health, fit
the orfe is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler forfeits fishing rights at a spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' reads as an adverb in the surface, as in fishing well, but here it is the adjective meaning healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a claim as a penalty is to lose one's entitlement to it.

clue.text: Rush back to one in German market

indicators.note: back means the word for rush is read backwards

parts.note: to dart is to rush suddenly
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: Someone hurries back to a German bazaar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DART into TRAD; 'to' joins it to EIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade in goods is to deal in and sell them commercially.

clue.text: It's a characteristic feature for a shallow container, some say

indicators.note: some say means some speakers pronounce it this way, signalling a word heard rather than read

parts.note: a tray is a flat, shallow holder

explanation.surface: A flat serving dish is said to be distinctive.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the word is often said like 'tray', with a silent final T; 'some say' allows for those who sound the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguishing quality or attribute of a person is a mark of their character.

clue.text: One allows rouge, finally, in child's kit of dressing utensils

indicators.note: the three pieces go inside the word for child

parts.note: a tot is a small child
one as the Roman numeral I
lets means allows

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A youngster's make-up box lets in some blusher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One allows' reads as a phrase, but it splits in two. 'finally' takes the last letter of 'rouge'.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching set of brush, comb and mirror for a dressing table is a grooming kit.

clue.text: It's used in an engine, dispersed into drops

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fuel is sprayed in droplets inside a motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersed' rearranges INTODROPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The rod joining a piston to the crankshaft is a moving part of a motor.

clue.text: The bird's with the musician

parts.note: the 's gives the letter S
and means with, together with
a piper is a musician who plays pipes

explanation.surface: A bird is in company with a bagpiper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bird's' looks like one unit, but the 's breaks off to give S.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading shorebird of the snipe family is a bird.

clue.text: It jogs one's memory about a surplus book

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: a reminder prompts recall

explanation.surface: A note prompts someone about an unwanted volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts REMINDER round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsold stock of a book sold off cheaply is excess copies.

clue.text: It's sinful getting a lot of money on the game

parts.note: bad means wicked or sinful
a mint is a huge sum of money

explanation.surface: Gambling a fortune on a match is wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock.
explanation.definitionFit: Shuttlecock-and-racket sport is one kind of game.

clue.text: Bird, having pinched one car, turned up in the East End, penniless

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means the letters read from bottom to top
having pinched means the bird holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a cob is a male swan
one as the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thieving bird steals a car and turns up broke in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having pinched' puts ICAR inside COB, making CICAROB; 'turned up' reverses it. Boracic lint is Cockney rhyming slang for skint, broke; the East End is London's Cockney heartland.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang: boracic lint stands for skint, meaning without money.

clue.text: Mother's about to acknowledge a wanderer

indicators.note: about means round, so the word for acknowledge goes round the word for mother

parts.note: to nod is to acknowledge with a dip of the head
ma is mother, and the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A mother is about to greet a traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to acknowledge' reads like 'about to' plus a verb, but 'about' is the container signal, and 'to acknowledge' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with no fixed home who moves from place to place is a roamer.

clue.text: Sort of jacket put on by principal

parts.note: to don is to put on clothes
key means chief or principal

explanation.surface: The headteacher slips into a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: A donkey jacket is a heavy workman's coat with a leather or PVC panel across the shoulders, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey jacket is a thick, short coat worn by labourers.

clue.text: Concerned with having clothing correct

parts.note: re means about or concerning
dress is clothing

explanation.surface: Someone worries about wearing the proper outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to set it right or remedy it.

clue.text: There's gravity in sad funeral song

indicators.note: the symbol is put inside the word for sad

parts.note: dire means dreadful or grim, sad
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A mournful hymn has a solemn tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gravity' suggests solemnity, but it is the physics symbol G.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a lament sung at a burial.

clue.text: Mark on female's neckwear

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: A woman covers a blemish on her neck with clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A length of fabric worn round the throat is an item worn at the neck.

clue.text: Tonic's taken in the right quantity

indicators.note: taken in means the letter is held inside the word for tonic

parts.note: a potion is a medicinal drink, a tonic; the 's reads as 'has'
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A medicine is swallowed in the proper dose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' puts R inside POTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is a share or amount of something.

clue.text: Modernise Scottish town without foreign money

indicators.note: without means the money is removed from the town's name

parts.note: Renfrew is a town near Glasgow
FR is the abbreviation for the franc, a foreign currency

explanation.surface: A Scottish town modernises without overseas investment.
explanation.walkthrough: Renfrew is a town in west-central Scotland; 'without' removes FR (franc).
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to restore it or bring it up to date.

clue.text: Cheat, and an eccentric gets bitter

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person
sharp means acid or bitter in taste

explanation.surface: A swindler and an oddball turn sour.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler who wins at cards by trickery is a cheat.

clue.text: Prod German captivated by unclad figure

indicators.note: captivated by means held inside, so the nude figure holds the letter

parts.note: a nude is a figure without clothes in art

explanation.surface: A German is enthralled by an undressed model and pokes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivated by' puts G inside NUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge is to poke or push gently.

clue.text: A box containing pencils in the chiffonier

parts.note: a chest is a large box
of means containing, as in 'a box of matches'
pencils are things that draw, drawers

explanation.surface: An artist keeps a box of pencils in a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pencils' are read as 'drawers', things that draw.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiffonier is a tall piece of furniture with a set of storage compartments.
